Three files, one name

PR playground for #4050. A one-line change, found by nearly reporting the wrong diagnosis.

What the log looked like

[RUN] test-fault-arms.sh          [PASS] (1s)   ← tests/manifests
[RUN] test-fault-arms.sh          [PASS]        ← tests/plugins
[RUN] test-fault-arms.sh          [FAIL] (11s)  ← tests/ci

Failed tests:
  - test-fault-arms.sh            which one?

Three different files, three different gate lists, one label. The summary names a file without saying which.

How it actually bit

Triaging a real review block, I grepped the job log, found the first test-fault-arms.sh entry passing in 1s, saw the failing gate absent from its list, and was about to report that the gate had never run.

The real failure was the third entry, eleven seconds later in the same log. First-match reads green while a different file of the same name is red. A human and an agent make that mistake identically, because both triage from the same text.

The fix is one line, twice

- test_name=$(basename "$test_file")
+ test_name="$test_file"

- FAILED_TESTS+=("$(basename "$test_file")")
+ FAILED_TESTS+=("$test_file")

The path was already in hand. Discarding it is what created the ambiguity. This fixes the class: the next duplicate is distinguishable the day it appears, with no rule to remember and no list to keep current. Renaming the three files fixes only today's collision; forbidding duplicate basenames adds a rule to enforce when the runner is simply throwing information away.

The assertion that would have proved nothing

The test plants two same-named files in two subdirectories and checks the summary names the failing path. My first version grepped the whole output for it, which the earlier [RUN] and [FAIL] lines already satisfy. It would have passed while testing nothing new.

It is now anchored to the Failed tests: block, and a second fault arm proves the difference: reverting only the summary site must still go red.

ARM 1  revert BOTH sites to basename       went red
ARM 2  revert ONLY the summary site        went red  ← the one that matters
restored                                   green, 3/3

Run it

bash tests/ci/test-runner-labels-by-path.sh
Exactly one duplicated basename exists across tests/ today. Small blast radius, and nothing stopped the next one.
